title: Online Paint Sales
one_liner: US online paint sales remain a growing but competitive e-commerce niche tied to repainting, home improvement, contractor demand and digital fulfillment.
overview: The Online Paint Sales industry includes internet sales of interior paint, exterior paint, stains, varnishes, protective coatings, painting supplies and related tools to households, DIY consumers, painters, contractors and small businesses. The 2021 baseline report placed 2020 revenue at $7.3 billion and forecast 2025 revenue of $8.3 billion, implying mid-single-digit pandemic-era growth followed by slower normalization. By 2025-2026, the category is still benefiting from broader online retail growth: US retail e-commerce reached $316.1 billion in Q4 2025 and $326.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 9.8% year over year in Q1 2026. However, paint demand is more cyclical than general e-commerce because repainting and coating projects depend on home sales, remodeling budgets, housing starts, professional contractor backlogs and consumer confidence.

key_stats.market_size: 2026 estimated US online paint sales revenue: $8.5 billion
key_stats.growth: 2020-2026 estimated CAGR: 2.4%; 2026 revenue growth is estimated near 2.0%-3.0%
key_stats.ecommerce_tailwind: US retail e-commerce sales were $326.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 9.8% from Q1 2025 and equal to 16.9% of total retail sales
key_stats.baseline_forecast: The baseline report forecast 2025 online paint sales revenue of $8.3 billion
key_stats.profit_margin: Baseline forecast 2025 EBIT margin: 3.8% of revenue
key_stats.establishments: Baseline forecast 2025 establishments: about 5,385; enterprises: about 2,139
key_stats.category_mix_2020: Interior paint 36.4%, exterior paint 22.9%, stains/varnishes/protective coatings 21.2%, supplies 13.4%, equipment 6.1% of revenue

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022 estimated revenue: $7.7 billion, calculated from the baseline 2020 revenue of $7.3 billion and the baseline 2020-2025 forecast CAGR of about 2.4%
baseline_2022.growth: 2022 estimated annual growth: about 2.4% under the baseline forecast path
baseline_2022.context: The 2022 baseline sits after the 2020 DIY/e-commerce surge but before the full impact of 2023-2025 housing affordability pressure and softer DIY traffic.

how_it_makes_money: Operators earn revenue by selling paint, stains, varnishes, primers, coatings, brushes, rollers, tape, drop cloths and other painting supplies through websites, mobile apps and marketplaces. Large retailers monetize omnichannel transactions through ship-to-home, buy-online-pick-up-in-store and Pro account ordering, while niche paint brands earn higher gross margins from direct-to-consumer color curation, samples, premium formulations and bundled supplies. Contractors and repeat Pro buyers are valuable because they place larger, more frequent orders and buy replenishment products.
cost_structure: Purchases are the largest cost, covering paint and coatings sourced from manufacturers or wholesalers, pigments, resins, containers and private-label inventory. Fulfillment costs are unusually important because gallons of paint are heavy, bulky, spill-sensitive and sometimes regulated for transport. Labor includes customer service, color consultation, merchandising, warehouse handling, IT and web operations. Marketing and paid search are significant because consumers compare color, price and reviews across Home Depot, Lowe's, Amazon, Sherwin-Williams, specialty retailers and direct-to-consumer brands. Profit is pressured by free shipping, returns, sample programs, price matching and sales-tax compliance across states.
current_dynamics: The industry is growing slower than broad e-commerce because paint is a tactile and project-driven product: shoppers still want color confidence, local availability and expert advice. Home Depot reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $164.7 billion and online sales equal to 15.9% of net sales, while Lowe's reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $86.3 billion and said online sales positively contributed about 105 basis points to comparable sales. In 2026, big-box retailers are leaning into online marketplace expansion, Pro loyalty, jobsite delivery and faster fulfillment. Paint manufacturers are using pricing, premium formulations and color tools to offset uneven unit demand. Sherwin-Williams reported 2025 net sales of $23.57 billion and said core North America DIY demand remained soft, while its Paint Stores Group improved in residential repaint and commercial end markets.
whats_growing: Online ordering, mobile color tools, sample kits, premium low-VOC and certified paints, Pro account replenishment, marketplace assortment, direct-to-consumer curated brands, ship-to-home accessories and buy-online-pick-up-in-store paint projects are growing. Retailers with large store networks are also growing digitally because local stores double as fulfillment nodes for heavy products.
whats_shrinking: Impulse DIY repaint projects, low-margin commodity gallon sales, pure-play models that rely on subsidized shipping, undifferentiated online paint stores and demand tied to new residential construction are weaker. New residential paint demand remains pressured by affordability constraints and slower housing turnover, while consumers are more selective on discretionary home projects.
recent_developments: 2024-12-11: Lowe's announced its 2025 Total Home Strategy, including accelerated online sales and the first US home improvement product marketplace.
2025-05-21: Lowe's announced a Mirakl partnership to scale Lowe's Marketplace for DIY and Pro customers.
2026-01-29: Sherwin-Williams reported 2025 net sales of $23.57 billion and noted soft core North America DIY demand.
2026-03-10: US Census data showed Q4 2025 retail e-commerce sales of about $316.1 billion and 16.6% of total retail sales.
2026-05-18: US Census reported Q1 2026 retail e-commerce sales of $326.7 billion, up 9.8% year over year.
2026-05-19: Home Depot reported Q1 fiscal 2026 sales of $41.8 billion and a fourth straight quarter of double-digit year-over-year online comparable sales growth.
outlook: Revenue is expected to keep rising through 2026, but growth should be moderate rather than pandemic-like. A reasonable 2026 estimate is $8.5 billion, with upside if lower mortgage rates revive existing-home turnover, remodeling and contractor workloads. The most defensible operators will be omnichannel retailers and specialized brands that reduce purchase friction through accurate color visualization, samples, local pickup, reliable tinting, Pro pricing and transparent delivery. Margin expansion will remain difficult because shipping, returns, customer acquisition and marketplace competition offset the benefits of e-commerce scale.
one_sentence: In 2026, US online paint sales are estimated at about $8.5 billion, supported by rising e-commerce penetration but constrained by soft DIY demand, housing affordability pressure and high shipping/service costs.

title: Online Payment Processing Software Developers
one_liner: Developers of payment gateways, merchant acquiring software, digital wallets and payment APIs continue to benefit from rising e-commerce, embedded finance and instant-payment adoption, while fee pressure, fraud risk and regulation intensify.
overview: This industry comprises companies that develop software used to authorize, route, settle, manage and analyze online payments for merchants, platforms, marketplaces, financial institutions and consumers. The baseline IBIS file put 2021 US industry revenue at $28.0 billion and forecast revenue to reach $34.1 billion by 2026, implying a 2025 revenue estimate of about $32.7 billion on the original 2021-2026 trajectory. Demand in 2025-2026 is being shaped by steady e-commerce penetration, platform and ISV-led payment distribution, digital-wallet use, faster ACH and instant-payment rails, and merchant demand for fraud, orchestration, billing, tax, identity and analytics tools around the transaction.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 estimated US industry revenue: $32.7 billion, derived from the baseline 2021 revenue of $28.0 billion and 2026 forecast of $34.1 billion.
key_stats.growth: 2025 estimated industry revenue growth: about 4.0%, consistent with the baseline 2021-2026 forecast CAGR.
key_stats.ecommerce_sales: 2025 US retail e-commerce sales: $1.2337 trillion, up 5.4% from 2024; e-commerce was 16.4% of 2025 total retail sales.
key_stats.latest_ecommerce_quarter: Q1 2026 US retail e-commerce sales: $326.7 billion seasonally adjusted, up 9.8% from Q1 2025 and equal to 16.9% of total retail sales.
key_stats.payments_activity: 2024 US noncash payments: 236.6 billion transactions; cards represented more than three quarters of transactions by number, while ACH represented nearly three quarters of value.
key_stats.fednow_adoption: 2025 FedNow year-in-review: 1,600 participating financial institutions, 44 certified service providers and 645% year-over-year volume growth from Q3 2024 to Q3 2025.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022 estimated US industry revenue: $29.1 billion, derived from the baseline 2021 revenue of $28.0 billion and the 2021-2026 forecast CAGR of about 4.0%.
baseline_2022.growth: 2022 estimated revenue growth: about 4.0% under the baseline forecast path.
baseline_2022.ecommerce_context: 2022 US retail e-commerce sales: $1.0341 trillion, up 7.7% from 2021; e-commerce was 14.6% of 2022 total retail sales.
baseline_2022.baseline_source_note: The baseline file was last updated August 16, 2021 and reported 2021 revenue of $28.0 billion, 2021 profit margin of 9.3%, and a 2026 revenue forecast of $34.1 billion.

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes mainly from merchant and platform fees tied to payment volume, including per-transaction charges, percentage take rates, gateway fees, authorization and settlement fees, currency conversion, instant-transfer fees, chargeback and risk tools, recurring SaaS subscriptions, billing and invoicing modules, fraud and identity products, data analytics, embedded lending and value-added financial services. Large processors also earn revenue from cross-border payments, wallet funding and defunding, account-to-account payments, card issuing support and merchant working-capital products.
cost_structure: Major costs include network and interchange pass-throughs, transaction processing infrastructure, cloud hosting, fraud and credit losses, compliance and risk operations, customer support, product engineering, sales and marketing, partner incentives, data-security controls and general administration. The baseline file reported a 2021 profit margin of 9.3% and forecast margin compression to 8.4% by 2026 as competition and fee pressure rise. Public 2025 disclosures show the scale of infrastructure costs: PayPal 2025 operating expenses rose 2% as transaction expense and transaction and credit losses increased, while Fiserv reported 2025 adjusted operating margins of 37.0% in Merchant Solutions and 45.3% in Financial Solutions.
major_players: PayPal Holdings: 2025 net revenue was $33.172 billion, US revenue was $18.868 billion and total payment volume was $1.79 trillion.
Stripe: businesses running on Stripe generated $1.9 trillion in 2025 payment volume, up 34% from 2024, and Stripe reported more than 5 million businesses on its platform.
Block/Square/Cash App: 2025 gross profit was $10.4 billion, with Cash App gross profit of $6.3 billion and Square gross profit of $3.9 billion.
Fiserv: 2025 GAAP revenue was $21.19 billion, up 4%, with 2025 organic revenue growth of 6% in Merchant Solutions.
Adyen: published its 2025 annual report in March 2026 and continues to compete as a global payments platform for enterprises including Meta, Uber, H&M, eBay and Microsoft.
Visa Acceptance Solutions/Authorize.net: Visa’s 2025 net revenue was $40.0 billion, processed transactions were 257.5 billion and value-added services revenue was $10.9 billion.
current_dynamics: The industry is still expanding, but the sources of growth are shifting from basic online checkout toward embedded payments, vertical SaaS, payment orchestration, fraud and identity tools, subscription billing, pay-by-bank, instant disbursements and cross-border commerce. US retail e-commerce grew 5.4% in 2025 and Q1 2026 e-commerce grew 9.8% year over year, keeping online checkout volume healthy. At the same time, processors face fee compression from merchant bargaining power, pay-by-bank alternatives, network incentives, growing fraud costs and scrutiny over deplatforming, BNPL compliance and open-banking data access.
whats_growing: Embedded payments through software platforms and ISVs are growing quickly; McKinsey estimated 2025 US payment-processing revenue through ISVs at $16 billion, up from $6.5 billion in 2020. Instant payments are growing, with FedNow reporting 1,600 participating financial institutions in 2025 and a 645% volume increase from Q3 2024 to Q3 2025. Fraud, identity and risk services are also expanding, shown by Visa’s 2025 value-added services revenue rising 24% to $10.9 billion. Cross-border, subscription billing, tax automation, revenue recognition, marketplace payouts and wallet defunding remain strong product areas.
whats_shrinking: Standalone gateway functionality is becoming less differentiated as merchants buy broader payment, software and financial-services suites. Check payments and cash withdrawals continue to decline in the US payments mix, reducing demand for legacy paper-payment workflows. Basic card-not-present processing margins are under pressure from intense competition, larger merchants negotiating rates, payment orchestration, pay-by-bank alternatives and rising fraud-management requirements. Crypto payment acceptance remains a niche merchant use case compared with cards, ACH, wallets and account-to-account payments.
recent_developments: 2025-04-03: Visa announced new value-added services including a reimagined Authorize.net, Unified Checkout and ARIC Risk Hub for acquirers, payment facilitators and merchants.
2025-07-07: The Federal Reserve published analysis on US pay-by-bank, noting low current adoption but growing interest from younger and higher-income consumers and potential merchant cost benefits.
2025-08-22: The CFPB released an advance notice reconsidering parts of the 2024 Personal Financial Data Rights open-banking rule, including representatives, fees, data security and privacy.
2025-09-09: Federal Reserve Financial Services said the FedNow transaction limit would rise from $1 million to $10 million in November 2025 to support higher-value commercial use cases.
2026-02-24: Stripe said businesses running on Stripe generated $1.9 trillion in 2025 volume, up 34% from 2024, and announced a tender offer at a $159 billion valuation.
2026-05-18: The Census Bureau reported Q1 2026 US retail e-commerce sales of $326.7 billion, up 9.8% from Q1 2025 and equal to 16.9% of total retail sales.
outlook: The industry outlook for 2026 is positive but more competitive than the pandemic-era acceleration period. Baseline revenue was forecast to reach $34.1 billion in 2026, and current demand indicators support continued growth: e-commerce penetration is rising, instant-payment infrastructure is scaling, and large merchants and platforms are buying more fraud, billing, orchestration and embedded-finance capabilities. Growth will be moderated by take-rate compression, merchant efforts to bypass card costs through pay-by-bank, regulatory uncertainty around open banking and BNPL, and cybersecurity and card-not-present fraud risks. Winners are likely to be processors with scale, bank and platform distribution, high authorization performance, strong fraud tooling, developer-friendly APIs and value-added software that makes switching costly.
themes: Fee compression and merchant bargaining power
one_sentence: The US online payment processing software developer industry is a growth-stage fintech software market whose 2025 revenue is estimated at about $32.7 billion, supported by $1.2337 trillion in 2025 US retail e-commerce sales and expanding card, ACH, wallet, pay-by-bank and platform-payment volumes.

title: Online Perfume & Cosmetic Sales
one_liner: Online beauty retailers are still gaining share as skincare replenishment, fragrance gifting, social commerce and omnichannel loyalty offset higher tariff and compliance costs.
overview: This industry includes companies that sell perfume, makeup, skincare and related cosmetic products online, including pure-play ecommerce retailers, brand-owned direct-to-consumer sites, marketplaces and the ecommerce arms of store-based retailers. The 2022 IBISWorld baseline placed industry revenue at $16.032 billion, with skincare at 61.8% of sales, cosmetics at 24.3% and fragrances at 13.9%. By 2025-2026, demand is being shaped by repeat-purchase skincare, prestige fragrance gifting, social commerce discovery, loyalty programs, virtual try-on tools and tighter regulation under MoCRA. Growth is positive but more normalized than the pandemic-era ecommerce surge, while price competition, returns, paid media costs, shipping costs and tariffs pressure margins.

key_stats.profit_margin: 2026 estimated operating/profit margin: about 6%-7%, broadly in line with the 2022 baseline margin of 6.4%
key_stats.ecommerce_context: U.S. retail ecommerce sales were $326.7 billion in Q1 2026, up 9.8% year over year, and ecommerce accounted for 16.9% of total retail sales
key_stats.beauty_context: U.S. prestige beauty sales reached $36.0 billion in 2025, up 4%; U.S. mass beauty sales reached $72.7 billion in 2025, up 5%
key_stats.top_online_stores: In 2025, sephora.com generated $3.458 billion in U.S. beauty ecommerce net sales, ulta.com $2.455 billion, bathandbodyworks.com $1.379 billion, fragrancenet.com $578 million and ilmakiage.com $526 million

how_it_makes_money: Operators earn revenue from online sales of skincare, makeup, fragrance, beauty tools and related cosmetic products. Sales flow through owned ecommerce sites and apps, third-party marketplaces, subscription/replenishment programs, loyalty programs, influencer and affiliate links, social-commerce shops, and omnichannel services such as buy-online-pick-up-in-store and ship-from-store. Margin comes from merchandise markups, private-label products, exclusive brand launches, data-driven promotions, subscriptions, marketplace fees and lower store labor intensity than traditional specialty retail.

cost_structure.purchases: Largest cost, covering branded inventory, private-label goods, packaging and imported inputs; 2025-2026 tariffs lifted landed costs for many China-sourced cosmetics and beauty products.
cost_structure.fulfillment_and_shipping: Material cost for warehousing, pick-pack, parcel delivery, returns processing, free-shipping thresholds and same-day delivery partnerships.
cost_structure.marketing: High and rising cost center, including paid search, social ads, creator commissions, affiliate fees, sampling, loyalty offers and promotional discounting.
cost_structure.technology: Website, mobile app, personalization, virtual try-on, fraud prevention, payment processing, CRM and cybersecurity costs.
cost_structure.wages: Baseline 2022 wages were $724 million, equal to about 4.5% of revenue; online operators require fewer selling-floor workers but need fulfillment, customer service, merchandising, data and digital marketing labor.
cost_structure.compliance: MoCRA registration, product listing, safety substantiation, adverse-event tracking, labeling, ingredient data management and state-level requirements add 2025-2026 overhead.
cost_structure.profit: Baseline 2022 profit margin was 6.4%; 2026 margins are pressured by tariffs, returns, acquisition costs and promotions but supported by premium fragrance, skincare replenishment and private label.

current_dynamics: The industry is benefiting from broad 2025 beauty resilience: Circana reported U.S. prestige beauty sales up 4% to $36.0 billion and mass beauty up 5% to $72.7 billion. Online demand is strongest where replenishment, reviews, creator content and loyalty programs reduce trial friction. Sephora and Ulta remain dominant specialty ecommerce destinations, while Amazon, Walmart and Target compete on convenience and price. The sector is also absorbing 2025-2026 cost shocks from tariffs, higher parcel fulfillment costs and MoCRA compliance. Consumer behavior is bifurcated: shoppers trade up for prestige fragrance, clinical skincare and devices, while also seeking mass-price dupes, minis, bundles and discounts.
whats_growing: Clinical and functional skincare, including dermatologist-backed, barrier-repair, SPF, acne and sensitive-skin products
Prestige and mass fragrance, with 2025 prestige fragrance up 5% and mass fragrance up 15% according to Circana
Lip products, minis, gift sets, body sprays and hybrid makeup-skincare formats
Social commerce and creator-led discovery, especially TikTok Shop, livestream selling and affiliate storefronts
Omnichannel loyalty programs, buy-online-pick-up-in-store, ship-from-store and same-day delivery
K-beauty, value prestige and direct-to-consumer brands with strong online communities
whats_shrinking: Purely undifferentiated discount ecommerce stores without brand trust or fast fulfillment
Online sales of shade-sensitive makeup where consumers still prefer in-store testing unless buying repeat items
Low-margin import-heavy products exposed to 2025-2026 tariff increases
Fragrance and cosmetics listings with weak authenticity controls, as marketplaces and brands tighten anti-counterfeit enforcement
Organic reach on social platforms, increasing reliance on paid creators and affiliate commissions
recent_developments: 2025-05-02: CBP ended duty-free de minimis treatment for China-origin low-value ecommerce shipments, raising costs for import-heavy beauty sellers.
2025-12-29: FDA released its MoCRA-mandated PFAS cosmetics report, highlighting data gaps and keeping ingredient scrutiny elevated.
2026-02-10: Circana reported 2025 U.S. prestige beauty sales of $36.0 billion, up 4%, and mass beauty sales of $72.7 billion, up 5%.
2026-03-10: Census reported Q4 2025 U.S. retail ecommerce sales of $316.1 billion, up 5.3% year over year, with ecommerce at 16.6% of retail sales.
2026-04-28: Statista/ecommerceDB ranked sephora.com first among U.S. beauty online stores in 2025 with $3.458 billion in net sales, followed by ulta.com at $2.455 billion.
2026-05-18: Census reported Q1 2026 U.S. retail ecommerce sales of $326.7 billion, up 9.8% year over year, with ecommerce at 16.9% of retail sales.
outlook: Revenue is expected to keep rising through 2026-2028, but at a mid-single-to-low-single digit pace for the narrow online perfume, cosmetics and skincare retailer segment as ecommerce penetration matures. Growth will come from skincare replenishment, prestige fragrance, mass fragrance, social commerce, mobile apps, loyalty data and faster fulfillment. Margin performance will depend on tariff mitigation, private-label mix, returns control, media efficiency and compliance execution. The most defensible operators will pair online convenience with trusted brands, authenticated inventory, product education, personalization and omnichannel services; weaker pure-play sellers will face high customer acquisition costs and price competition from marketplaces and specialty chains.
themes: Value-seeking and premiumization at the same time
one_sentence: The U.S. Online Perfume & Cosmetic Sales industry sells skincare, makeup and fragrance through websites, apps, marketplaces and omnichannel retailer platforms, with 2026 revenue estimated at $17.8 billion after a 2025 beauty-market rebound and continued growth in U.S. ecommerce penetration.

title: Online Pet Food & Pet Supply Sales
one_liner: Online pet food and pet supply sellers are benefiting from recurring food demand, autoship habits and expanding pet ownership, but competition from Amazon, Walmart, Petco, PetSmart and grocery channels keeps price pressure high.
overview: This industry sells pet food, treats, litter, toys, accessories, health supplies and medications through websites, apps and digital marketplaces. The baseline 2022 IBIS framing described a COVID-accelerated e-commerce market that had reached $17.4 billion in 2021 after 11.3% growth, with pet food and treats accounting for 56.0% of revenue and pet supplies 36.0%. By 2025-2026, the channel has matured: growth is less about first-time online adoption and more about autoship, convenience, broad assortment, pharmacy and health products, private labels, and omnichannel fulfillment. Current APPA data show the total US pet industry reached $158 billion in 2025, up 3.7%, with 2026 projected at $165 billion, while Deep Market Insights estimates the US online pet food and supplies market at $20.45 billion in 2025. Consumers are still protecting core pet budgets, but value seeking, promotions and trade-down pressure are more visible than during the pandemic surge.

key_stats.market_size: 2025: $20.45 billion US online pet food and supplies market; 2026: US pet industry expenditures projected at $165 billion across all channels and categories.
key_stats.growth: 2026-2034 forecast CAGR: 7.76% for the US online pet food and supplies market; 2025 total US pet industry spending grew 3.7% and 2026 total pet industry growth is projected near 4.4%.
key_stats.pet_ownership: 2025: 95 million US households owned at least one pet; 71 million households owned a dog and 53 million owned a cat.
key_stats.online_penetration: 2025: 53% of pet parents purchased pet products online versus 45% in-store; 2025 online pet purchases were led by pet food at 83% of online pet buyers, treats at 80%, and vitamins/supplements at 55%.
key_stats.subscription_behavior: 2025: 49% of pet parents reported subscription-based purchasing, down from 52% in 2024; food remained the top subscription category at 30% of consumers.
key_stats.category_context: 2025: US pet food and treats sales reached $68.3 billion, supplies/live animals/OTC medicines reached $34.4 billion, and total US pet retail sales reached $158 billion.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022: about $18.2 billion implied from the January 2022 IBISWorld baseline, which reported 2021 revenue of $17.4 billion and projected $21.4 billion by 2026.
baseline_2022.growth: 2022: about 4.3% implied annual growth under the 2021-2026 IBISWorld forecast; the baseline cited 11.3% growth in 2021 and a 4.3% 2021-2026 revenue CAGR.
baseline_2022.profit_margin: 2021: 4.1% EBIT margin in the baseline; 2026 baseline projection: 4.0%.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2021 baseline revenue mix: pet food and treats 56.0%, pet supplies 36.0%, pet medications and treatments 1.7%, other 6.3%.

how_it_makes_money: Operators earn revenue from online sales of branded and private-label pet food, treats, litter, toys, bedding, collars, leashes, bowls, carriers, aquariums, grooming supplies, OTC health products and prescription medications. The strongest economics come from repeat consumables, autoship subscriptions, larger baskets, private brands, vendor-funded promotion, loyalty programs, pharmacy relationships and app-based retention. Shipping fees, membership-style benefits and cross-selling health, insurance or veterinary services can add revenue, but most sales still come from physical goods.
cost_structure: Major costs are merchandise purchases and inbound freight, parcel delivery and fulfillment labor, warehouse operations, payment processing, technology platforms, customer service, advertising, promotions and returns. Margins are constrained by heavy consumable products that are costly to ship, transparent online price comparison, free-shipping thresholds, discounting, and competition from mass merchants. Profitability improves with private-label penetration, higher autoship retention, better inventory turns, supplier allowances, warehouse automation and dense last-mile delivery coverage.
current_dynamics: The market is still expanding but has normalized from the pandemic spike. Chewy remains the defining pure-play operator, reporting fiscal 2025 net sales of $12.60 billion and Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales of $3.36 billion, up 7.7% year over year, with autoship reaching 84.4% of Q1 2026 net sales. Online share is being reinforced by recurring food, treats and supplements, while brick-and-mortar chains are using stores, grooming, vet clinics, curbside pickup and loyalty programs to defend share. Consumers are buying essentials, but inflation and household budget pressure are pushing more deal seeking, private-label trial and promotional shopping.
whats_growing: Autoship and repeat delivery, premium and veterinary diets, cat products, vitamins and supplements, pharmacy and pet health products, private-label food and supplies, app-based loyalty, omnichannel pickup and delivery, and accessories tied to pet wellness and enrichment are growing. APPA reported 2025 cat ownership rose 5% year over year to 53 million households, and Deep Market Insights identifies accessories as the fastest-growing product type over the forecast period.
whats_shrinking: Pandemic-era growth rates, impulse discretionary accessories, low-differentiation hard goods, subscription usage rates, and standalone online retailers without fulfillment scale are under pressure. In 2025, 22% of pet owners reported spending less on pets, up from 20% in 2024, and subscription-based purchasing fell to 49% from 52% in 2024. Omnichannel competitors are also pulling some demand back toward stores for immediate-need purchases, services and bundled trips.
recent_developments: 2026-03-11: Petco reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $6.0 billion, down 2.5%, and guided fiscal 2026 net sales to flat to up 1.5%.
2026-03-25: Chewy reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $12.60 billion, up 6.2% year over year, or 8.3% on a normalized 52-week basis.
2026-03-26: APPA reported US pet industry expenditures reached $158 billion in 2025, up 3.7%, and projected $165 billion for 2026.
2026-04-02: APPA purchasing data showed 53% of pet parents bought pet products online in 2025, up from 51% in 2024.
2026-04-08: Deep Market Insights estimated the US online pet food and supplies market at $20.45 billion in 2025 with a 7.76% 2026-2034 CAGR.
2026-06-10: Chewy reported Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales of $3.36 billion, up 7.7%, with autoship at 84.4% of net sales.
outlook: The industry should keep outgrowing the broader pet market through 2026 because food, treats and health products are frequent, replenishment-driven purchases that fit subscription and delivery models. Growth will be steadier than the 2020-2021 surge, with real gains coming from household pet ownership, cat growth, pharmacy, subscriptions, data-driven personalization and omnichannel convenience. Key risks are shipping costs, promotion intensity, mass-merchant price competition, consumer trade-down, and the difficulty of profitably shipping bulky low-margin consumables.
one_sentence: The US online pet food and pet supply market is a growth retail channel anchored by repeat consumables and subscription delivery, with 2025 market size estimated at $20.45 billion and growth supported by 95 million pet-owning US households in 2025.

title: Online Photo Printing
one_liner: A mature e-commerce printing niche where smartphone photo volumes support demand for personalized books, cards, wall art and gifts, while standard print volumes keep drifting lower.
overview: The US online photo printing industry sells digital-photo output ordered through websites and apps, including standard prints, photo books, cards, calendars, wall decor and personalized gifts. The baseline IBISWorld file described a pandemic-era lift from nostalgia and keepsakes, followed by slower growth as online ordering became mainstream. Current 2025-2026 signals point to a split market: standard photo-print volumes remain mature, but higher-value products, AI-assisted photo-book creation, mobile ordering and same-day pickup are supporting revenue per order. Market-size estimates vary by scope: IBISWorld's public 2024 page put US online photo printing at $4.3 billion, while other 2025-2026 research pages use narrower or broader definitions for online photo printing and digital/photo-merchandise markets.

key_stats.market_size: 2025: about $3.02B for US online photo printing in one 2026 market estimate; 2024: $4.3B in IBISWorld's public US online photo printing market-size page.
key_stats.growth: 2025: 3.35% CAGR cited for the US online photo printing market by IndustryResearch.biz; 2024: IBISWorld's public page showed -0.4% annual market-size growth.
key_stats.online_channel_share: 2025: online platforms accounted for 61.05% of global photo-printing revenue in Mordor Intelligence's photo printing market coverage.
key_stats.snapfish_sales: 2025: Snapfish.com annual online-store sales estimated at $318.3M by Grips, down 10-20% from 2024; May 2026 sales estimated at $26.5M.
key_stats.traditional_print_revenue: 2026: US traditional photo-print revenue forecast above $1.4B by Rise Above Research, rising to over $1.6B by 2029 despite declining print volumes.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022: about $3.36B, inferred from the baseline file's 2021 revenue of $3.317B and its 2021-2027 projected CAGR near 1.23%.
baseline_2022.growth: 2022: about 1.2%-1.3%, based on the baseline file's post-2021 projected growth rate.
baseline_2022.establishments: 2021 baseline: 549 establishments; 2027 baseline projected growth rate: 1.12% CAGR.

how_it_makes_money: Selling standard photo prints ordered online or through mobile apps.
Selling higher-ticket photo books, cards, calendars, canvases, wall decor and personalized gifts.
Charging for premium paper, layflat books, larger formats, rush production, shipping and add-on design services.
Serving professional photographers, schools and enterprises with recurring or bulk print programs.
Using promotions, subscriptions, app engagement and seasonal events to convert stored digital photos into physical products.

cost_structure.labor: Meaningful but partly offset by automation; baseline wages were $791M in 2021, about 23.8% of baseline 2021 revenue.
cost_structure.materials: Paper, ink, photo substrates, canvas, mugs, packaging and other print inputs are major variable costs; paper-price inflation remains a margin risk.
cost_structure.fulfillment: Shipping, postal services, local delivery and store-pickup logistics are central because most orders are fulfilled remotely or through retail partners.
cost_structure.technology: Platforms need continuing spending on apps, upload/storage systems, editing tools, AI-assisted design and production workflow software.
cost_structure.marketing: High promotional intensity is structural, especially around holidays, weddings, graduations and gift seasons.
cost_structure.profit: Baseline 2021 profit margin was 6.3%, with only modest expansion forecast to 6.4% by 2026.

current_dynamics: Competition is intense because consumers can choose pure-play online brands, retailer photo sites, pharmacy pickup, professional labs and do-it-yourself digital sharing. The strongest operators are pushing customers toward premium products with better margins, such as photo books, wall decor, cards and personalized gifts. AI-assisted curation and auto-layout tools are reducing the friction of turning large camera rolls into orderable products. Retail fulfillment remains important because Walgreens and similar chains can offer same-day pickup for online and mobile orders, while pure-play brands compete on design tools, quality and promotions. Persistent discounting keeps pressure on margins, and lower standard-print volumes are being offset mostly through price increases and mix shift.
whats_growing: Photo books, especially AI-assisted and mobile-created albums.
Wall decor, canvas, metal, wood panels and other premium substrates.
Personalized gifts, cards, calendars, blankets, mugs and seasonal keepsakes.
Mobile app ordering, camera-roll import and one-click album creation.
Same-day pickup and local fulfillment for prints, cards and decor.
Average revenue per print as paper, ink and fulfillment costs lift prices.
whats_shrinking: Traditional walk-in photofinishing demand not integrated with online ordering.
Consumer willingness to print every photo rather than curate smaller sets.
Undifferentiated online print-only offers that compete mainly on coupons.
Calendar and routine paper-photo demand where digital substitutes are sufficient.
recent_developments: 2024-08: IBISWorld's public market-size page listed US online photo printing at $4.3B in 2024, down 0.4%.
2025-08: Rise Above Research forecast US traditional photo-print revenue to rise from over $1.4B in 2026 to over $1.6B by 2029, while volumes decline at a -2.7% CAGR.
2025-10: Shutterfly named Emily Whittaker, formerly a VistaPrint executive, as CEO and emphasized AI capabilities and a new technology platform.
2026-02: Mixbook described its app-exclusive Memories feature, using AI to organize camera-roll photos into ready-to-use albums.
2026-05: Grips estimated Snapfish.com generated $26.5M in May 2026 online sales and $318.3M in 2025 annual online-store sales.
2026-06: Mixbook updated guidance for Auto-Create, an AI-assisted workflow that places selected photos into book templates.
outlook: The industry should remain mature rather than high-growth, with revenue supported by premiumization, AI-assisted creation, mobile ordering and fulfillment convenience. Standard photo prints are likely to keep losing volume, but operators can defend revenue through higher average prices, better merchandising and a mix shift into books, cards, wall decor and gifts. The main risks are promotion-driven price competition, paper and shipping costs, weak discretionary spending and the continued adequacy of free digital sharing. The winners through 2026-2029 will be platforms that reduce creation friction, use customer photo libraries effectively and run efficient automated production at scale.
one_sentence: Online photo printers let consumers and professional photographers upload digital images, customize products and receive prints or photo merchandise by delivery or store pickup.
